\tributehead{\tributetitle{Tribute to My Beloved Husband, My Darling 'D'}}{}
\begin{tribute}
\tributephoto{plates/tributes/franco-nero-and-pauline}{40.0mm}{28.7mm}
How do i put into words how i truly feel about losing a man i spent 50 years
(49 years married) of my life with?

My D. My Crown, My Cover and My Best Friend..

Franco Nero as he fondly liked to be called was the husband of my youth. He
was my pillar - A man of great strength and resilience. He was my personal
comedian filled with endless humour, and my number one supporter in life who
proudly supported me every step of the way. When it involved me and his
children, my husband spared no one and was willing to face anyone who dared
to stand against us.

He was my hero, my confidant and with him by my side, i knew I could move
mountains and together we achieved a lot. My husband loved sports,
particularly football, he was a loyal fan of Arsenal and he used to enjoy
watching live matches at the stadium. He loved good food, and he had a very
sweet tooth. He was a devout Catholic and a great lover of Mother Mary. He
made me a huge fan of the Holy Rosary which became a guiding light, not just
for me, but for our entire family.

His demise has left a big vacuum in my life, in the lives of the Atsekhameh
family and all those he left behind, but I am consoled by the fact that he
was called on the 15th day of August - On the feast of assumption of our
Mother Mary, whom he loved and adored so dearly, and i'm even more at peace
because i know she came to lead you gently into the arms of her beloved Son.

The house feels so empty without you Uyemhe, and my heart breaks knowing I
will never see your face or hear your sweet voice again. I know there will
be moments when I will instinctively call on you just to give you random
gists. I miss us singing together, and how you always backed me up whenever
I randomly started a song. You really loved singing enjoyed dancing, but i'm
happy you're dancing with the Angels now -I hope you tell them all your many
stories, and show them your writing skills. One special talent you had was
the ability to make people laugh without trying and diffuse any situation
with your unique sense of humour, I hope you're making them laugh too.

I truly wish life gave us more conversations, more singing and dancing, more
gists, more laughter, and more TIME.

I love you my Sweet Guy, and i miss you so much.

Thank you for being my HUSBAND

Your life was truly a gift.

Your memories are a treasure.

And your love is a legacy that will never die.

Rest well, my ADEOKWILE

Rest well, FRANCO NERO INTERNATIONAL

\tributesignoff{Love Always,\\Your Darling D.\\Your beautiful wife\\Your forever BEST FRIEND.\\Lady Pauline Charity Atsekhameh}

\end{tribute}

\tributedivider

\tributehead{\tributetitle{Tribute to My Father Sir Francis Atsekhameh}\\\tributetitle{(Franco Nero Intl)}}{}
\begin{tribute}
You never truly realize the value of a moment until it becomes a memory.

A rush of memories came flooding the moment I received the news of your
demise, so intense that it kept me awake for almost 72hrs. The pain was
deep, the reality was heartbreaking. I'd never see my Franco Nero alive
again.

My earliest memories of life was all about you. The playfulness, the
laughter, the songs. I even remember the first time I went to school in
nursery one, Franco Nero had me on his shoulders. My first bicycle lessons,
my first bike ride, I still remember the first of many times you took me to
Ogbe stadium to watch your beloved Bendel Insurance FC.

That fueled my passion for football that has stuck till date, we were always
going to the home games.

Daddy will always carry me on his shoulders into the stadium, protecting me
from the crowd surge. That thought me a valuable lesson in love at that
early age. You do everything in life to protect the ones you truly love and
cherish.

My love for reading came from you at that young age. Daddy made me read the
newspapers at age six. I went through his entire collection of novels before
I finished primary school. Talking about dozens and dozens of books that
were way beyond my tender age at the time. He always encouraged and
motivated me to be a voracious reader. A trait I still carry till this day.

Daddy also shaped my love for music too, his collection of vinyl records was
a collectors delight any day. That turn table brought so much joy to the
family on a daily basis.

Your strict discipline taught me to make the right choices in life and stay
on the straight and narrow path. I knew pretty early in life not to take
anything that wasn't mine, even by mistake. You taught me early about
accountability and that all actions had consequences, whether good or bad.

Franco Nero was firm in a loving kind of way. You just knew not to go doing
wrong things out there because he would protect you publicly but reprimand
you in private. Those lessons shaped my personality to this day, gave me the
knowledge of good or evil and the choice to make every single time.

As you got older and softer, I really got to appreciate you better for all
the lessons I didn't realize at the time that had gone ahead to shape my
lifestyle and choices.

Thank you for teaching me that integrity always wins over short cuts. I
became a better man because I was raised by you daddy. Valuable lessons that
we take for granted in life. I remember all our conversations on my last
visit and I promise to step into the big vacuum you left and be there for
mom, my younger siblings and all your grandchildren going forward. I accept
the responsibility and hope to excel in my new role with God's help.

Farewell Sir Francis Onoteagbor Atsekhameh, our very own Franco Nero. You
always called yourself the Sky man, we know you'll always protect and watch
over us from the Skies in the company of the Angels and Saints.

Thank you for life and everything daddy, probably didn't say it as much as I
should have done every day. Till we meet again on resurrection morning,
journey well Sir.

\tributesignoff{Your Son,\\Solomon Osigbemeh Atsekhameh 001.}

\end{tribute}

\tributedivider

\tributehead{\tributetitle{A Tribute to Daddy}}{}
\begin{tribute}
Daddy was a perfect example of someone who truly practised Psalm 55:22 ,
casting his burdens on the Lord and trusting Him completely.

He always had a word of wisdom for every situation, but what made Daddy
special was the way he delivered it. He would subtly drop a profound piece
of advice, often disguised as a joke, and leave you thinking about it long
after the conversation.

If you wanted to get Daddy's full attention, all you needed to do was
express your love for his mother, Mama Mary. Once you mentioned Mama Mary,
you had his passcode! His love and devotion to God, and his deep reverence
for Mother Mary, were evident in the way he lived his life. Mother Mary was
always his go-to rescue.

His grandchildren will forever remember his jovial spirit, especially during
our Sunday-Sunday catch-up calls. Those little moments of laughter, teasing,
and conversation have created precious memories that will stay with us
forever.

Daddy, we love you, and we will miss you so much. I honestly cannot imagine
a Benin house without you. Your presence filled that home in a way that
words cannot fully describe.

Thank you for the wisdom, the laughter, the prayers, and the beautiful
memories.

Keep resting in God's bosom, Daddy.

You will forever remain in our hearts.

\tributesignoff{Your Daughter,\\Omolola Uyemhe Atsekhameh}

\end{tribute}

\tributedivider

\tributehead{\tributetitle{A Tribute to My Father Sir Francis Onoteagbor Atsekhameh}}{}
\begin{tribute}
Francis Onoteagbor Atsekhameh a.k.a Franco Nero was a good father who lived
a great and fulfilled life. He raised a great family with his wife Pauline
Charity Atsekhameh and together they had five wonderful children, raised in
a very Catholic and christian way.

He always taught us to be united, have the fear of God, and honour our
mother Mary who has always interceded for the family in all ramifications.
He was also a legionary who believed in praying the rosary to strengthen our
faith and unite our family in Christ Jesus. We will miss Daddy and we are
very grateful for all he did for the growth of the entire Atsekhameh family.
We know you have gone to be with our heavenly Father, our mother Mary and
our Lord Jesus Christ.

Your beloved children will miss you so much.

\tributeprayer{Adieu Daddy,\\Adieu Franco Nero, Adieu Francis Onoteagbor Atsekhameh}

\tributesignoff{Your Son,\\David Eshemokhai Atsekhameh}

\end{tribute}

\tributedivider

\tributehead{\tributetitle{A Befitting Tribute to My Beloved Dad}}{}
\begin{tribute}
\tributephoto{plates/tributes/franco-nero-and-emma}{40.0mm}{29.8mm}
Today, I celebrate the life of an exceptional man, a loving father, a
devoted Christian, and a man whose presence brought warmth and joy to
everyone around him.

My Dad was a disciplined devoted husband/father and a man of faith. He loved
God deeply and held a special devotion to Mother Mary. His faith was not
merely something he professed; it was reflected in the way he lived, treated
people, and carried himself. He trusted in God and sought to live a life
worthy of His love and mercy.

Professionally, Dad was an astute and gifted salesman. He had a remarkable
ability to connect with people, understand them, and earn their trust. His
interpersonal skills, confidence, determination, and natural charm made him
exceptional at what he did. But beyond the profession was a man who valued
people and relationships. To those who knew him, he was much more than a
salesman---he was a friend, a confidant, and a man whose word could be
trusted.

Dad was also a jovial and cheerful man. He had a wonderful sense of humour
and could light up a room with his presence. His laughter, jokes,
conversations, and infectious personality created memories that will remain
with us forever. Even in difficult moments, he had a way of bringing smiles
to people's faces.

And then there was his love for sports. Dad enjoyed football and wrestling,
and these were more than mere pastimes for him. They were opportunities for
excitement, conversation, and shared moments with family and friends. His
passion for football was particularly memorable because he was a staunch
supporter of our beloved Arsenal Football Club. Supporting Arsenal was
something he embraced wholeheartedly---with all the emotions, debates,
celebrations, disappointments, and unwavering loyalty that come with being a
true football fan.

Dad, you lived a life filled with faith, hard work, laughter, friendship,
family, and passion. You touched many lives in ways you may never have fully
realised. Your departure has left a space that cannot be filled, but the
memories you created and the values you passed on will continue to live
through us.

We will remember your smile.

We will remember your humour.

We will remember your love for God and Mother Mary.

We will remember the salesman who could win people over with his words and
personality.

We will remember the sports lover who could get caught up in the excitement
of a football match or wrestling bout.

And, of course, we will remember the proud Arsenal supporter who remained
loyal through the highs and lows.

Dad, your earthly journey has ended, but your story continues in the hearts
of all who loved you.

As we mourn your passing, we also give thanks to God for the gift of your
life and for the privilege of having you as our father.

May God Almighty, whom you loved and served, receive your soul. May the
Blessed Virgin Mary, to whom you were devoted, intercede for you and lead
you gently into eternal rest.

Rest peacefully, Dad.

You will always be loved.

You will always be remembered.

You will forever remain a part of us.

\tributeprayer{Eternal rest grant unto him, O Lord,\\and let perpetual light shine upon him.\\May his soul, and the souls of all the faithful departed,\\through the mercy of God, rest in peace.\\Amen.}

Until we meet again, Dad---rest well.

And from wherever you are, keep an eye on us all and watch Arsenal defend
the league I am glad you saw us win after more than two decades before
passing. Journey well Franco Nero.

\tributesignoff{Your fellow Arsenal lover,\\Emma ``Boogie'' Atsekhameh}

\end{tribute}

\tributedivider

\tributehead{\tributetitle{Tribute to My Father-in-Law, Francis Atsekhameh}}{}
\begin{tribute}
It is with a heart filled with sadness, gratitude and faith that I pay
tribute to my dear father-in-law, Francis Atsekhameh. His passing has left a
space in our family that words cannot fully describe, yet we are comforted
by the life he lived and by the hope we have in Christ.

He was a devoted Catholic whose faith was not merely a title, but an
important part of who he was. His devotion reminds us that our earthly
journey is temporary and that the promise of eternal life belongs to those
who place their trust in God.

As a husband, father, father-in-law and grandfather, he occupied a cherished
place in our family. We thank God for the years we were privileged to share
with him and for the family legacy that continues through his children and
grandchildren. Though we grieve because we can no longer see him, we remain
grateful that he was part of our lives.

The words of Scripture give us comfort:

\tributeprayer{``I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in me, though he die, yet shall he live.'' (John 11:25).}

We therefore entrust him into the loving and merciful hands of God,
believing that death is not the end but a passage into eternal rest.

Dear Daddy, may the Lord forgive every human failing, reward your faith and
receive your soul into His heavenly kingdom. May Our Lady, whom you honoured
as a Catholic, intercede for you, and may the angels lead you into paradise.

You will be remembered with love, spoken of with gratitude and carried
always in our hearts. Rest peacefully, Francis Atsekhameh. Until we meet
again in the presence of God.

\tributesignoff{Eternal rest grant unto him, O Lord,\\and let perpetual light shine upon him.\\May his soul rest in perfect peace. Amen.\\[\baselineskip]Your daughter in-law,\\Katie Emesomiade Atsekhameh}

\end{tribute}

\tributedivider

\tributehead{\tributetitle{A Tribute to My Beloved Father, Franco Nero - The Great!}}{}
\begin{tribute}
A Tribute to My Beloved Father, Franco Nero - The Great!

A great tree has fallen, but the roots he planted run deep within us.

Saying goodbye to you, dad, is the hardest thing I have ever had to do. You
were not just my father; you were my personal hype man, always hailing me
and calling me ``my handsome son,'' my first teacher, my number one
disciplinarian who moulded me with cain.

Franco Nero was a man of quiet strength, immense integrity, and boundless
love with the cain right beside him.

He taught me the value of hard work, honesty, and generosity. Growing up, he
would always invite us to dine with him, and he loved sharing his meat even
when you didn't eat with him.

Daddy had a unique way of guiding you, not through loud lectures but with
discipline. He had this exceptional belief he vested in me that gave me the
courage to keep going.

Daddy was a great story teller, he knows how to hold you down with gists of
him from the past. You have to give it to Franco Nero for having the gift of
cracking you up with laughter.

August 15th is a day I will always remember. It's been a few weeks, Dad, but
I don't think I have accepted that I won't see you again. Though your
physical presence is gone, your memories live on.

I will take solace in the memories we created, the laughter we shared, and
the love that will never fade.

Thank you for everything\dots{} Your \textit{``ALAWADA''} misses you
greatly.

\tributeprayer{Rest in peace, Franco Nero, the great.}

\tributesignoff{Your Fine Son,\\Peter Egiegba Atsekhameh}

\end{tribute}

\tributehead{\tributetitle{Tribute to My Pops}\\\tributetitle{``FRANCO NERO INTERNATIONAL'' a.k.a SKYMAN a.k.a DJANGO!!!}}{My Daddy\dots{} My Daddy\dots{} My Popz \& My ``GUYEST'' Guy\dots{}}
\begin{tribute}
\tributephoto{plates/tributes/franco-nero-and-emike}{28.5mm}{38.0mm}
\tributedropcap{H}{is} name was Francis Onoteagbor Atsekhameh, but as a
young man, he decided simply being called Francis wasn't enough, so he named
himself ``FRANCO NERO INTERNATIONAL'' and insisted that everyone,
irrespective of age, called him that.

That was my Daddy! A character, strong-headed, confident, unconventional,
and completely unapologetic about who he was.

My Popz loved sports, especially football and wrestling, and he was a
diehard ARSENAL fan, so much that for someone who loved food, he would be so
unhappy and refuse to eat whenever Arsenal lost a match. LOL

My Pops was a really tough guy, but underneath all that, was a man with one
of the best senses of humour who would literally crack everyone up without
even trying.

In his fit days, he loved to walk, to sing, and above all, he absolutely
loved dancing, and with him, no good music was ever allowed to go to waste.

He was also an incredibly gifted writer, with an exceptional command of
English, and was always the secretary in every organisation he found
himself. One thing about him was the fact that he'd never let a grammatical
error go unnoticed, cos he always found a way to correct you with humour and
sarcasm.

He loved good conversations, good music, storytelling, and good company, but
whenever Mum was around, his world was complete.

Dad was a man of many talents, he was an astute salesman --- a talent and
trait I proudly inherited from him. He also had a natural curiosity about
languages, and he spoke English, Etsako and Yoruba fluently.

He could gist for days, and recount events from decades ago, like it was
yesterday. He remembered dates and details in a way that amazed everyone,
even in his ailing days when his memory began to fail him in so many ways.

One of his greatest gifts to me is my love for good music, because from a
very young age, he introduced me to some of the greatest musical legends ---
Michael Jackson, Madonna, Millicent Small, Kenny Rogers, The Everly
Brothers, and so many others. He gave me an appreciation for good music that
has stayed with me throughout my life. One memory I will forever cherish was
when he first wrote out on a piece of paper the lyrics of ``Take a Message
to Mary'' for me, and together we would sing aloud.

My Daddy and I had a very unique relationship, and like every authentic
relationship, it wasn't always perfect. I made sure he said ``SORRY, PLEASE
and THANK YOU'' whenever it was required, and sometimes he would literally
chase me around the house repeatedly telling me ``thank you o'' whenever i
insisted. Despite our differences, I was somehow still the ONLY person who
could make him change his mind when he would sometimes prove difficult and
refuse listening to anyone else. Yes, we had our fights and sometimes
disagreed, but against all odds, my Daddy remained my ``GUYEST'' Guy, and i
was his favourite GIRL!

Whenever we saw each other or talked on the phone, man had a special way of
reminding me exactly who I was to him.

He would always start with:

``Is that my Emike?''

And then proceed to call me ``EMIKE de EMIKE'' repeatedly, making me laugh
so hard.

He would sing my praises, pray for me, and remind me that I would always be
his beautiful girl.

He was a staunch Catholic, whose love for God ran deep, but his love for
Mother Mary was enviable and truly special. He didn't stop at honouring her;
he identified proudly as her son, and referred to her as ``MAMMA MARY my
mother''.

Even in your most difficult times and lowest days, you prayed the ROSARY
without ceasing, and even when you couldn't pray, you made sure to always
have it on you.

And then came the day you left us.

The 15th day of August, my August!

The very day the Catholic Church celebrates the Feast of the Assumption of
the Blessed Virgin Mary into Heaven -A day that commemorates the belief that
when Mary ended her earthly life, God took her body and soul up into heaven.

To some, this may simply be a coincidence.

But to me --- and to everyone who truly knew you and witnessed your
extraordinary devotion to her --- it feels like something much deeper, and
we believe your mother came to take you home.

Perhaps, after all those years of calling her Mother, she answered when it
was finally time for you to go home.

Daddy, I am deeply honoured that you found me worthy of entrusting your
final wishes, and I am even more honoured that your children are fulfilling
them. Aunty Ivy is doing an excellent job too. She's truly making you proud.

We know you're smiling down on us because your beloved wife and children did
not let you down.

My only request to you now is that you Take the BEST care of Mummy, as she
did you during your time here on earth. Continue to be her guardian angel,
watch over her, comfort her, protect her and guide her until the day you
both meet again, never to part anymore.

I know Mummy misses you terribly.

We all do\dots{} because there is now a silence where your voice used to be.

A space where your stories and laughter used to fill.

Thank you my GUY.

Thank you for the lessons, the laughter, the music, the stories, the dance
moves, the prayers and even the disagreements.

Thank you for introducing me to the beautiful things that shaped the lady I
am today.

Thank you for the parts of yourself that lives on in me.

Your work here is done Popz.

No more worries about Arsenal.

No more grammatical errors to correct.

No more dinners to boycott after an Arsenal defeat.

No more health battles.

No more pain.

Just pure peace.

Until we meet again\dots{} keep resting in the bosom of the Lord, my SKY
MAN, and enjoy the loving arms of your Mother Mary.

Adieu, Pops.

\tributesignoff{Yours Truly,\\``Emike De Emike''\\``Your Omosi No Ni 20 Ezao''}

\end{tribute}

\tributedivider

\tributehead{\tributetitle{In Loving Memory of a Man Who Made a House a Home to All}}{}
\begin{tribute}
There are people who cross our paths during childhood and leave an indelible
mark in our lives. For me, Sir Francis Onoteagbor Atsekhameh was exactly
that person.

Growing up, some of my absolute favorite memories were the holidays I spent
staying over at the Atsekhameh's house. From the moment I walked through the
door, he never made me feel like just a guest he treated me like one of his
own. He created a home filled with warmth, laughter, and a sense of safety
that I will carry with me forever.

Whether it was his welcoming smile, the quiet wisdom he shared, or the
subtle ways he looked out for us while we were busy being kids, his presence
was a constant anchor. He taught us, through his actions, what it means to
be generous, kind, and deeply devoted to family.

To my Dear friend and sister Emike and the entire family, i thank you for
sharing your precious Dad with me. The incredible qualities you carry every
day are a living testament to the wonderful man he was. He may no longer be
with us, but the shelter, joy, and love he provided during those
unforgettable childhood holidays will live on in my heart forever.

\tributeprayer{Rest in peace FRANCO NERO, You are deeply missed.}

\tributesignoff{Love Always,\\Your Non-Biological Last Born\\Esther Iredia}

\end{tribute}

\tributedivider

\tributehead{\tributetitle{Tribute to Grandpa Benin}}{}
\begin{tribute}
\tributephoto{plates/tributes/franco-nero-and-treasure-n-princeton}{28.2mm}{38.0mm}
I have never met a man who loved animals as much as Grandpa did. I will
always remember our first trip to the Benin house. There were chickens and
two dogs named Brownie and Bingo. Grandpa loved taking care of them. He
would feed the chickens and always made sure their cage was properly locked.
He even let us bathe the dogs once!

These little moments showed us how caring, patient, and loving Grandpa was.
He had such a joyful heart, and being around him always made us happy.

Whenever Grandpa called us on the phone, he was always so happy to hear our
voices. He would pray for us and tell us to do great things in life and make
him proud. Those prayers and words will always stay in our hearts. I pray
that his prayers will continue to follow us as we grow and become the people
he wanted us to be.

Grandpa, we will miss your smile, your joyful heart, your prayers, and all
the beautiful memories you gave us.

\tributeprayer{Rest peacefully, Grandpa. We love you, and we will miss you so much.}

\tributesignoff{Your Lovely Grandchildren,\\Treasure \& Princeton}

\end{tribute}

\tributedivider

\tributehead{\tributetitle{Our Tribute to Grandpa}}{}
\begin{tribute}
\tributephoto{plates/tributes/franco-nero-and-talia-n-tyshawn}{34.5mm}{38.0mm}
Dear Grandpa,

It is difficult to say goodbye to you. We wish we could have more time with
you, but we are thankful to God that you were our grandpa and that you will
always be part of our family story.

We will remember you with love. Even though we cannot see you anymore, you
will remain in our hearts, in our prayers and in the memories our family
shares about you.

Grandpa, we promise that we will do our best to grow into children you would
be proud of. We will love and support one another, respect our family, work
hard, remain humble and keep God at the centre of our lives. We will carry
the Atsekhameh name with honour and allow the good things you stood for to
continue through us.

As you go to rest, we pray that God welcomes you into heaven and gives you
eternal peace. This is not goodbye forever, because our faith teaches us
that we shall meet again.

Rest well, Grandpa. We love you, we will miss you, and we will never forget
you.

Our promise We will honour Grandpa by loving God, loving our family, working
hard and living in a way that would make him proud.

May his soul, and the souls of all the faithful departed,

through the mercy of God, rest in peace. Amen.

\tributesignoff{With all our love,\\Talia \& Tyshawn}

\end{tribute}

\tributehead{\tributetitle{Dear Daddy Franco Nero}}{}
\begin{tribute}
Writing a eulogy about you was not part of my feasibility plans for this
year. Never in my wildest imagination did I think that I would be called
upon to put pen to paper to speak of your life in the past tense. I was
completely taken aback on the 19th of August at about 9:31 p.m. when I
received the devastating news of your passing. It was one of those moments
that leaves the mind numb and the heart struggling to accept reality. Even
now, it feels surreal to write these words, knowing that a man whose
presence brought warmth, wisdom, and strength to so many is no longer
physically with us.

Today, as I attempt to find words adequate enough to honor you, I am
reminded of how difficult it is to summarize a life that meant so much to so
many people. Some lives are measured by the years they lived, but yours is
measured by the countless hearts you touched, the lives you uplifted, and
the enduring memories you created.

You were more than a father, mentor, and friend. You were a beacon of
humility, grace, and kindness. You possessed that rare ability to make
everyone around you feel valued and important. Your words carried wisdom,
your actions reflected integrity, and your life exemplified the virtues of
selflessness and genuine compassion.

Daddy Franco Nero, you lived a life that spoke louder than words. You
possessed the remarkable gift of making everyone feel important. Whether
interacting with family, friends, neighbors, or complete strangers, you
treated people with dignity and respect. You never measured people by their
social status, accomplishments, or possessions. Instead, you saw humanity
first, and that was one of the many things that made you exceptional.

Your life was a practical demonstration of selflessness. You gave without
expecting anything in return. You listened without judging. You counseled
without condemning. You helped without publicizing your acts of kindness.
The impact of those noble gestures may never be fully known because much of
what you did was done quietly, away from the spotlight, motivated only by a
sincere desire to make the lives of others better.

What made you truly remarkable was the way you combined strength with
gentleness. You were firm when circumstances demanded firmness, yet
compassionate when people needed understanding. You were a man of
conviction, but never one of arrogance. You stood for what was right, not
because it was popular, but because it was right. In your own unique way,
you taught us that true greatness lies not in power, wealth, or influence,
but in character, humility, and service to others.

One of the greatest legacies you leave behind is not found in material
possessions or worldly achievements, but in the countless lives you touched.
The love, encouragement, and guidance you freely gave have left an indelible
mark on hearts far and wide. Many will remember your kindness; others will
remember your wisdom. But all who encountered you will remember a man whose
life reflected authenticity, strength, and an unwavering commitment to doing
good.

It is often said that some people come into our lives and quietly leave
footprints on our hearts. Daddy Franco Nero did far more than that. He left
a trail of inspiration, hope, and cherished memories that will continue to
guide those privileged to have known him. Though death has taken him from
our sight, it can never erase the impact of a life so beautifully lived.

As we mourn this painful loss, we also celebrate a life that was rich in
purpose and abundant in love. We take comfort in the memories shared, the
lessons learned, and the values you instilled in all of us. Your physical
absence leaves an unfillable void, but your spirit will forever remain alive
in the hearts of your family, friends, and all whose lives you enriched.

Farewell, Daddy Franco Nero.

Your race was well run. Your assignment was faithfully executed. Your
journey was marked by dignity, compassion, and purpose. The world may have
lost a remarkable soul, but Heaven has gained a noble one.

As the curtain falls on your earthly sojourn, your memory will continue to
shine like a beacon in our hearts. We will remember your smile, your wisdom,
your generosity, your unwavering humanity, and the countless ways you made
this world a better place.

Thank you for the privilege of knowing you. Thank you for the lessons you
taught without words. Thank you for the love you freely gave.

Sleep on, Daddy Franco Nero, in the bosom of the Almighty. Though gone from
our sight, you will never be gone from our hearts. Your legacy lives on,
your light continues to shine, and your memory shall forever remain blessed.

\tributeprayer{May your gentle and noble soul rest in perfect peace. Amen.}

\tributesignoff{Okhidemeh A.T. Richard}

\end{tribute}

\tributedivider

\tributehead{\tributetitle{Tribute for Sir. Francis Atsekhameh}}{}
\begin{tribute}
My dear Franco,

Your death came as a great shock to me. For over 60 years, I have known you,
from our childhood days in Apotse Quarters in Ivioghe Community.

What started as friendship grew into a bond that made you more like a
younger brother to me.

You were quite intelligent, hardworking, dependable, and a man of strong
faith.

Our families grew together, and our children grew up together. Your wife
became like a daughter to me and my late wife, and the bond between our
families remained stronger throughout the years. We were always there for
one another, in good times and in difficult moments.

I will deeply miss you and always remember the good years we shared. I thank
God for the privilege of knowing you for so many years.

May Almighty God grant your soul eternal rest and give your wife, children,
and the entire family the strength and comfort to bear this painful loss.

\tributeprayer{Rest well, my dear Franco, my friend and younger brother. You will always be remembered in Jesus' mighty name, AMEN.}

\tributesignoff{High Chief, Sir. Tom Iyelobu (KSJI)}

\end{tribute}

\tributedivider

\tributehead{\tributetitle{Tribute to Oluamhe Nekpe Kpe (My Inlaw, Who Is as Fine as the Tigers Skin)}}{}
\begin{tribute}
\tributephoto{plates/tributes/franco-nero-helena}{40.0mm}{26.7mm}
This my inlaw that we are bidding farewell, God, please take him to a good
place because when he was alive, we had such a wonderful relationship. He
never frowned at me or even got angry with me for once in my 50 years of
knowing him, and not for once did he ever wrong me. Every time I see him, I
will call him in form of praises saying ``OLUAMHE OLUAMHE'', and everytime
he will respond with smiles and a soft laughter saying ``that's me for
sure'', I will then call him by his native name ONOTEAGBOR, and he will
laugh and say, ``that's my name, na me be that, and ''yes I will live long
in this world". I pray that God receives his gentle soul, and help him rest
in a good place. He was a good man and as my inlaw, we lived well together
here on earth being married to my elder sister for almost 50 years. I will
miss him because we made lots of good memories always telling jokes and
laughing.

He will sometimes tell his wife that its been a while since he saw me. They
will get into the car and drive all the way to visit us on the other end of
town. Other times, I will go look for them, and when going, I will cook for
him as an elderly person, and upon arrival, I will call out to him
'OLUAMHE', I cooked Okorto (thick melon soup)for you. Okorto that you enjoy
very well.. I know God will grant him eternal rest because he's a good man.

My heart is broken especially because i can't express my pain knowing he is
gone forever. The day I came and saw him lying down with his back facing me,
I said to him OLUAMHE, is this you, who will now smile and laugh with me. I
was talking to him, and he responded, saying he could hear me and he's
laughing too. The next time I came, he didn't laugh with me or talk to me,
then it fully dawned on me that he was leaving us soon. He had never gotten
angry with me or I got angry with him for any reason. We always confided in
each other, and each time I come to tell him what troubles me, he will tell
me such is life, and I should please have patience.

Now I don't have anyone to share those jokes with.

I miss him so much, and I pray God keeps him in his bosom.

OLUAMHE! OLUAMHE!!

Mhe kho na! Who will I call OLUAMHE now???

ADIEU MY GOOD INLAW

Continue to rest in peace

\tributesignoff{Mrs. Helen Iyamokhe Otse (nee Bossey)}

\end{tribute}

\tributedivider

But if I had to say who my brother was in one sentence, I'd say my brother
was a great man of love, integrity and generosity.

He was an upright man, a role model and a mentor to me, my children and many
others.

I will forever miss him.

May the Lord welcome him into eternal Joy, grant him rest and may his gentle
soul rest in peace.

Adieu my beloved brother,,,

Adieu Onoteagbor, until the resurrection morning where we shall meet to part
no more.

\tributesignoff{Your Sister,\\Victoria Ikhianosime\\Nee Audu}

Your life was a blessing, your fatherly love and counsel was beyond measure,

Your last physical interaction with me in the hospital was so lovely that

Adieu beloved uncle with a golden heart!!!

I'll never forget the love you showed to me and my mother (Sister) as you
always called her, the way you cared for us when I needed a father in my
life you truly gave me fatherly love and everything I needed to be cared
for, the best a father could ever be.

You were a source of hope and compassion for so many, this legendary

Thank you for your fatherly love and inspiration. We continue to be indebted

May your sweet soul continue to rest peacefully in the bosom of the Lord
Amen!

\tributehead{\tributetitle{Farewell to My Father and My Inlaw}}{}
\begin{tribute}
\tributephoto{plates/tributes/franco-nero-and-bro-imonokha}{21.1mm}{38.0mm}
Our father that passed was a very nice man to everyone, especially our
family, the Bosseys. He was not just an inlaw but like a son to the family.

I remember when our father - Pa Matthias Ozimede Bossey, was alive, he
played the role of a son in Papa's life and even in his death, during the
burial and afterwards and he did an excellent job. That's why I stood
solidly by him when he lost his mother and made sure he had my full support
during her burial, because he was a very good man to us, and I couldn't
leave him to do it alone.

Beyond that, every time he sets eyes on me, he will always check in to say..
How are you my son? Even during Emike's wedding, when I visited his house,
we discussed a lot. He was fond of asking about everyone with genuine care,
patting you on the back as the caring man he was. He would always reach out
whenever he sees you and never act like he doesn't know you.

He was very very very caring.

Almighty God, who is the owner of this world, has said it is time for Daddy
to come to him, and by the grace of God, what we owe him now is a befitting
burial.

Sleep Well My In-law

\tributesignoff{Your Son,\\Mr. Imonokha Bossey}

\end{tribute}

\tributedivider

\tributehead{\tributetitle{A Tribute to Eramah}\\\tributetitle{(Franco Nero)}}{}
\begin{tribute}
Grandpa, it is hard to believe that you are no longer with us. On that
faithful day, 15th August 2026, the news of your death came with so much
cold taken all over my system

For the period I became close to him, he was joy and he was laughter. He was
a man who loved his children so much and cared for peaceful coexistence.He
was also a strong legionary and a committed member of the catholic church.
His faith was steady, his dedication was real, and he served with a heart
full of love.

He lived with so much happiness and he gave that happiness freely to
everyone around him. He was a man who loved good music and when deeply moved
he will stand up to dance. Grandpa was a man with so much energy when it
comes to praying the Rosary.

We will miss that energy, his warmth and his unwavering faith. Rest in peace
Sir FrancoNero, continue to dance with the angels.

We love you, and we will never forget you.

\tributesignoff{Your Extended Family,\\The Nwadialors'}

\end{tribute}

that Daddy has gone to rest with Lord. I am consoled because 'Erha mwan' you

Erha-mwan I will always remember your prayers for me anytime I visit you, we

\tributehead{\tributetitle{Tribute to My Dear in-Law, Francis Atsekhameh}}{}

My dear in-law, it is difficult to say goodbye. I fondly called you ``in-
law,'' and today, those simple words carry so much meaning.

Your passing leaves an empty place in our family. We would have wished for

As we mourn you, my heart is with your children, grandchildren and all those

Rest peacefully, my dear in-law, Francis Atsekhameh. May God grant you

\tributehead{\tributetitle{Tribute to Our Dearest Father-in-Law, Late Sir Francis O. Atsekhameh}}{}
\begin{tribute}
\tributephoto{plates/tributes/franco-nero-with-sir-n-lady-chinwo}{40.0mm}{26.7mm}
We, the Chinwo family of Rumuawhoechor Rumuekini Akpor LGA, River State,
received the news of your passing on with rude shock. We recall vividly in
October 2024 when we came for the marriage ceremony of your daughter, Emike
and our son Okechukwu. You participated actively in the rigours associated

that you couldn't survive 2026.

Nevertheless, God knows why you should leave us now. We can not question

surely miss you. We thank you for giving us your daughter, we promise that
this relationship with the Atsekhamehs will grow from strength to strength
by his grace.

\tributeprayer{Adieu our father-in-law and rest in the bosom of God, \\till we meet to part no more.}

I pray that God Almighty continue to comfort us in this moment of grief and

May your soul rest in peace.

\tributehead{\tributetitle{Tribute to Our Departed Member}}{by THE ASSOCIATION OF AUCHI CATHOLIC DIOCESE INDIGENES}
\begin{tribute}
\tributedropcap{I}{t} is with deep sorrow and a profound sense of loss that
the Association of Auchi Catholic Diocese Indigenes pays this tribute to our
dear brother, Sir. Francis Atsekhameh, whose death has left a painful void
in our Association, the Church and among all who had the privilege of
knowing him.

The news of his passing came to us with great sadness. Nevertheless, as
Christians, we are consoled by the assurance that for those who believe in
Christ, death is not the end, but a passage to eternal life.

As a member of our Association, Sir Francis Atsekhameh was a valued brother
whose presence, fellowship and contributions will remain fondly remembered.
He identified with the objectives and aspirations of the Association and
demonstrated the spirit of brotherhood, unity and mutual support which we
hold dear.

To his immediate family, relatives, friends and loved ones, we extend our
heartfelt condolences. We pray that God will grant you the strength and
fortitude to bear this irreparable loss. May the memories of his good deeds
and the positive impact he made during his lifetime remain a source of
comfort to you.

As an Association, we shall continue to cherish his memory and remember him
in our prayers and Holy Masses.

May your soul, and the souls of all the faithful departed, through the mercy
of God, rest in peace. Amen.

\tributesignoff{Signed: Lady G.E.T. Umolu\\Vice Chairman\\For: Chairman}

\end{tribute}

\tributedivider

\tributehead{\tributetitle{Tribute to Sir Francis Atsekhameh}}{A FORMER FINANCIAL SECRETARY OF THE SACRED HEART ZONE, ST. JUDE CATHOLIC CHURCH, IWOGBAN, BENIN CITY.}
\begin{tribute}
In Loving Memory of Our Dear Brother-in-Christ and Friend.

It is with profound sadness, but with gratitude to God Almighty for a life
well lived, that we pay tribute to our dear brother, Sir Francis Atsekhameh,
who served faithfully the Church and the Sacred Heart Zone of St. Jude
Catholic Church.

His death has left a deep void in our hearts and in the life of our
Christian community. Yet, as people of faith, we are consoled by the
knowledge that death is not the end but a transition to eternal life with
our Lord Jesus Christ.

During his time as Financial Secretary of the Sacred Heart Zone, he
demonstrated commendable dedication, honesty, diligence, and commitment to
the affairs of the Church and the Zone. He carried out his responsibilities
with a strong sense of accountability and service, understanding that his
position was not merely an office but an opportunity to contribute to the
growth of the Church and the welfare of God's people.

Beyond his official responsibilities, he will be remembered as a brother and
friend whose presence brought warmth and fellowship to those around him. His
commitment to the Church and his fellow parishioners earned him the respect
and affection of many.

Today, we mourn his passing, but we also celebrate his life and the legacy
of service he has left behind. The values of commitment, responsibility,
humility, and Christian brotherhood, which he exemplified, will remain an
enduring part of his memory.

As we bid him farewell, we are reminded of the words of St. Paul:

\tributeprayer{``I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.'' \\(2 Timothy 4:7)}

We pray that the Almighty God, whom he served through his commitment to the
Church and humanity, will receive his soul into His eternal kingdom.

May God forgive his earthly sins, reward his good deeds, and grant him
eternal rest.

To his family, we express our heartfelt sympathy and condolences to his wife
and children.

May the Blessed Virgin Mary, Queen of Heaven, intercede for him and comfort
all who mourn his departure.

Farewell, dear brother and faithful servant.

Until we meet again in the presence of our Lord.

ADIEU!!!.

\tributesignoff{Signed:\\Sir Peter Eboigbe-Uzzi, Ksp.\\Chairman, Sacred Heart Zone.}

\end{tribute}

\tributedivider

\tributehead{\tributetitle{Tribute to a Well Dedicated and Hardworking Legionary - Late Brother Francis Atsekhameh}}{}
\begin{tribute}
On self volition, you came to the Legion of Mary, got registered and
performed very well. With much interest displayed, dedication and hard-work,
you became the president of Our Lady Queen of Nigeria praesidium, St. Jude
Parish, Iwogban Benin city.

Our praesidium members today mourn your so soon demise. Nobody can question
God. We believe that he called you and you have answered. May he grant you
eternal rest in peace. Amen.

\tributesignoff{Brother James Abhieghonmhen\\On behalf of O/L Queen of Nigeria\\St Jude Parish, Benin City.}

\end{tribute}

\tributehead{\tributetitle{Tribute to Sir Francis Onoteagbor Atsekhameh}}{}
\begin{tribute}
\tributephoto{plates/tributes/ogie-of-ivioghe}{28.5mm}{38.0mm}
Greetings to the family of Sir. Francis Onoteagbor Atsekhameh on the demise
of your father.

It's not a bad thing for someone to pass on, when God says it's their time,
especially because he came, he saw and he conquered. There is nothing that
was done in this village that he didn't participate in. He had his eyes and
mind at home.

He was my brother and my father too, growing up, he used to cut our hair as
little children. May God let his soul find peace in this journey of
eternity.

Whatever good he left undone, it is my prayer that the children will carry
on from there. God will strengthen you all and give you good health. You
will not walk into a fight, and fight will not walk into you. You all will
be healthy, you will live long and you all will take care of your mum as you
did to your father. Good tidings are what you will have, as you come home to
lay him to rest, it is going to be smooth, no hindrance will be on the way.

I seize this medium to greet you all, as it really hurt me to hear of your
fathers death, but we know that God is the owner and giver of life.

Rest in peace, Father

\tributesignoff{From:\\Alhaji Chief Musa Omosimuah Emokhor\\THE OGIE OF IVIOGHE}

\end{tribute}
